question_text: Estimate the density of a cobalt-chrome alloy used for artificial-hip joints as a weighted average of the densities of constituent elements: $50 \mathrm{wt} \% \mathrm{Co}$, $20 \mathrm{wt} \% \mathrm{Cr}, 15 \mathrm{wt} \% \mathrm{~W}$, and $15 \mathrm{wt} \% \mathrm{Ni}$. Give your answer as the value of density.The unit of the answer is Mg/m^3.
response:
For a weight-fraction mixture, the alloy density is the harmonic weighted average:

$$\frac{1}{\rho} = \sum_i \frac{w_i}{\rho_i}$$

Using $\rho_{\rm Co}=8.90$, $\rho_{\rm Cr}=7.19$, $\rho_{\rm W}=19.25$, $\rho_{\rm Ni}=8.90$ (all in g/cm³ = Mg/m³):

$$\frac{1}{\rho} = \frac{0.50}{8.90}+\frac{0.20}{7.19}+\frac{0.15}{19.25}+\frac{0.15}{8.90} \approx 0.10864$$

$$\rho \approx 9.20\ \mathrm{Mg/m^3}$$

$$\boxed{9.2}$$
